title: Undated cipher letter, probably to Lorenzo de' Medici (ASF Mediceo avanti il Principato XLVIII 214r, catalogue 2309): the Siena no. 11 cipher identified, read in part with George Lasry's key (partial; partial reading explained)

steps.what: 16 lines, 787 tokens transcribed by shape in the sign names of targets/siena11; the sign set and the nulls g#, 31, 87 identified as those of Siena no. 11.

Sign-set coverage by four keys (Siena no. 11 96.4 %, LXXII 183 65.3 %, Dieci 1414 49.4 %, CXIX 117 39.0 %); Siena no. 11 and LXXII 183 tried on lines 1-5 (M5 0.1593 against 0.0000); Lasry's key chosen and frozen unchanged.
One pre-registered measurement on lines 6-16 of 2309 (no clear exists): Italian word measure M5 0.2335 against at most 0.0719 for 200 shuffled keys, margin 0.16 under 0.30: not validated.

Held-out test on another letter of the family, XLVIII 294 c. 306v l. 1-9, against its clear of the time c. 276 (amendment A1 declared): letter agreement 0.6419 against at most 0.2045 for 200 shuffled keys, margin 0.437; partial (0.85 not reached). The portion contains no 'PLUS ODAG', so the derived rule D1 was not exercised.
2309 read word by word with K_SIENA11_D1: 39 certain, 13 probable, 11 restored words, 45 unresolved stretches; about 35-40 % of the letter read.

Third pre-registered test, on a portion never used before: XLVIII 294 c. 306r lines 1-16 (411 cipher tokens) against the upper part of its clear c. 276r. Letter agreement 0.6519 against at most 0.1854 for 200 shuffled keys (partial again). Derived rule D1 ('PLUS ODAG' = c): 5 of its 6 occurrences align on 'c' in the clear, p = 0.005 against 200 random-position controls: held. Candidate values: TRI = 'che' held (4 of 5, p = 0.005); PLUS alone = o did not hold (0 of 3); PIBAR = n not testable (no occurrence).

2309 decoded again with K_SIENA11_D1_TRI (Lasry's key + D1 + TRI = che) and re-read: 46 certain, 13 probable, 11 restored words, 46 unresolved stretches (was 39 / 13 / 11 / 45); about 35-45 % of the letter read.

Integration check: the figures of tests 2 and 3 agree between validation.txt, the measure file, NOTES and the profile; not re-run (the clear copy c. 276 is not published). Whole-portion agreement gain from D1 is small (0.6519 with, 0.6390 without). Read share kept as certain + probable words only.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The sign set of 2309 matches Siena no. 11; George Lasry's key of that letter (targets/siena11) was applied unchanged, plus two single values derived later and held on a fresh portion (D1 'PLUS ODAG' = c, TRI = che). The key failed a test on 2309 itself and is partial on two held-out portions of a letter of the same family (XLVIII 294 against its clear c. 276).

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered tests (not docs/_validate.py). On 2309 itself: M5 0.2335 vs at most 0.0719 for 200 shuffled keys, margin 0.16 under 0.30: not met (failed). Held out on XLVIII 294 c. 306v against its contemporary clear c. 276: 0.6419 vs at most 0.2045, margin 0.437, under the 0.85 set in advance: partial. Third test 12 Nov 2026 on c. 306r (fresh) against c. 276r: 0.6519 vs at most 0.1854, partial; D1 ('PLUS ODAG' = c) held 5/6 and TRI = che 4/5 (p = 0.005 each, 200 random-position controls).

outcome.fraction_read_source: reading/xlviii214.md (12 Nov 2026): certain + probable words cover about 35 % of the 683 decoded letters, about 45 % with the restored words (10 Nov: 33 % and 43 % of 665); stated as about 35-45 %.

gaps.item: about 55-65 % of the letter (46 unresolved stretches, 11 restored words)
gaps.detail: the text decodes with the key but long stretches do not read as words; 13 sign forms of 2309 are not in the key (TRI now is); PIBAR = n and the nulls DIV, OO, ST are untested proposals

gaps.item: PLUS alone (aligned twice on 'c' in the 12 Nov test, after the pre-registered 'o' failed)
gaps.detail: needs another letter of the '##' family with a clear; XLVIII 294 is used up and XLVIII 158 is too short

gaps.item: the clear copy c. 276 of XLVIII 294, used for tests 2 and 3, is not published
gaps.detail: no one outside can repeat the tests; the ASF filza is the only source

gaps.item: key partial (0.6419 and 0.6519 against 0.85); transcription at 1272 px
gaps.detail: a higher-resolution image of XLVIII 214 from the ASF would settle doubtful forms
nothing on the leaf; conte Antonio and conte Carlo do not settle the date (1478-79 or 1482-85)

texts.label: ASF MAP XLVIII 214r, undated cipher letter (catalogue 2309)
texts.summary: Fragments of a letter, probably to Lorenzo de' Medici, about condottieri and their contracts: Count Antonio and Count Carlo, dealings in Venice, a sum of 15,000 ducats, a 'liberation', an intention of 'the lord'; one clear phrase 'Poi un altra volta'.

reading_review.note: Read word by word as Italian on 10 Nov 2026 with K_SIENA11_D1 (39 certain, 13 probable, 11 restored, 45 unresolved) and again on 12 Nov 2026 with K_SIENA11_D1_TRI: 46 certain, 13 probable, 11 restored words, 46 unresolved stretches, about 35-45 % read; read in part; key partial (failed on 2309; 0.6419 vs 0.2045 and 0.6519 vs 0.1854 held out on XLVIII 294); D1 and TRI = che held on a fresh portion.

outcome.notes: Partial reading explained. The key is George Lasry's; our part is the identification of the cipher of 2309, the transcription, the tests and the partial reading. No images (ASF): text only; the clear of c. 276 is not reproduced.

prior.where: No decipherment on the leaf or in the inventory; web search of 10 Nov 2026 found nothing on MAP XLVIII 214; Marco Vito's work concerns letters of 1486-1491; catalogue 2309 open, no target for it on origin/main.

human: Brice Dudout set the rules (each step pre-registered and hashed, thresholds fixed in advance, one measurement per test). AI agents compared the sign set with the known keys, transcribed, measured and read. No human palaeographer checked the transcription or the reading.
